segments: Chronography of Barhebraeus.
[a severe earthquake] in Nishapur,
and all its inhabitants went out into the plain,
and they remained for many days,
until it ceased, and then they returned.
And it also occurred in Khorasan,
but not as severely as in Nishapur.
And in the year one thousand five hundred and seventeen [of the Greeks],
606 of the Arabs (1209-1210 AD):
there was an agreement between al-Malik al-Adil and Nur al-Din Arslan Shah, the lord of Mosul.
And Nur al-Din gave his daughter to one of the sons of al-Adil,
and they agreed with one another to take Sinjar away from Qutb al-Din, its lord,
and that it should belong to al-Adil;
and that they would take the Island of Qardu (Jazirat Ibn Umar) from the son of Sinjar Shah, its lord,
and that it should belong to Nur al-Din.
And al-Adil prepared himself,
and came and took the Khabur and Nisibis, which belonged to the lord of Sinjar.
And when Nur al-Din heard this, he was shaken,
and became like a man sobered from his wine.
And he considered and realized that if [al-Adil] took Sinjar and the Island,
not only would he not give him the Island,
but he would even take Mosul from him {OCR? - text: but also from Mosul he would take from him}.
from him.
And when he took counsel with his wise men,
he was blamed by all of them for not letting them in on the secret before forging it with al-Adil.
And they said to him:
"Now you have no opportunity,
except to stand with him in that which you promised him.
Otherwise, he will make a pretext against you and come against you,
as against one who violates oaths."
And while he was being tossed about in this sea [of trouble],
and showing that he was preparing a force to send to the aid of al-Adil,
an envoy came to him by night from Muzaffar al-Din Gokburi, the lord of Erbil.
And he promised to gather his forces, come to him, and unite with him,
and not allow al-Adil's hand to enter these lands.
And Nur al-Din rejoiced with great joy,
and sent oaths to this effect.
And that very night the envoy went and informed Muzaffar al-Din,
and he gathered forces,
and without delay came and encamped outside Mosul.
And he sent an envoy to the Caliph,
that he might send [word] rebuking al-Adil for his greed.
And he sent an envoy to al-Malik al-Zahir, the son of Saladin, the lord of Aleppo,
and to the Sultan Izz al-Din Kaykaus,
and they all promised help.
For even those who were with al-Adil were not zealously fighting against Sinjar,
